logs: Review of jobs: Not a base to build on yet: 10 major and 10 minor findings, no blocker. In normal use the code works and the unit's 32 tests pass, but several promised behaviours fail when probed. (1) env start retries on the same port, not the next one. (2) Concurrent env starts can be given the same port, because ports.lock is released before the record is written. (3) The loud 'kept dying' failure is served a second time without measuring. (4) The one-restart cap is per call, so a job that dies later than one call's wait is restarted forever. (5) The alarm backstop has no handler, so a runaway job is restarted instead of failing on the time limit. (6) The time-limit message gives the wrong number and unit. (7) The crash and time-limit errors do not name the log. (8) The worker and attach both read, change and rewrite the job record without a lock, so a result can be served twice. (9, 10) Two tests cannot fail: the semaphore test and the nonce test both passed against mutants that removed the behaviour. The builder's two reported departures: keeping the log after a failed start is right; the non-inheritable lock is only partly right (S3R-jobs-11). Outcomes: AU-S2-12 left-for-builder is reasonable; P3REQ-06 left-for-builder is not, because the spec has not adopted the resolution. Findings are in /Users/jmagady/dev2/vsdd-factory/rewrite/findings/sources/extra-step3-jobs-review.json.. 20 findings, 10 blocker or major.
Round 1 for jobs: 18 of 20 fixes confirmed, 5 still open.
Round 2 for jobs: 3 of 6 fixes confirmed, 5 still open.

departures_from_plan: Plan 3.3 says the worker 'makes the lock descriptor non-inheritable'; the same invariant is achieved by the mechanism: pass_fds hands the descriptor to the worker, and PEP 446 defaults every other descriptor non-inheritable, so worker children (ctx.run, spawned with no pass_fds) never hold the lock (D3's observable contract holds).

Plan 3.5 implies nothing is left after a failed triple-port start; the implementation deliberately keeps the log file (deleting record and lock) so the error's log pointer names real evidence, and a later start truncates it.

fix.summary: All five findings fixed in the G1 (jobs) unit plus the AU-S2-12 ledger correction. C1-1: attach's loss branch killpg of command_pgid is now gated on a per-key cmd.lock the worker holds and its commands inherit through pass_fds, so a reused group id or pre-reboot number is never killed; the field is documented in rewrite/spec/records/job.md (plans are frozen for builders). C1-2: env._launch holds a per-key settle lock never passed to the product and writes the pid right after Popen; stop_products and _held_answer treat a starting record with a free settle lock as stale (stop by pid), leave a live start call alone, and keep the record of a product whose lock survives the KILL so its port stays taken. C1-3: admission measures the queued record at RECORD_CAP - RECORD_HEADROOM (new exported constant 128) and the worker's and env._launch's record writes fall back to a minimal record instead of dying at the cap. S3R-jobs-14: the two missing tests added. S3R-jobs-20: the five 'see conflicts/commands.md' pointers moved out of the design files into conflicts/commands.md (gaps 14 and 15 extended). Interface changes other units see: store gains <key>.cmd.lock and <key>.settle.lock swept by prune/_delete_key; JobContext gains optional cmd_lock_fd; jobs exports RECORD_HEADROOM; admission bar sits at RECORD_CAP - RECORD_HEADROOM; stop_products semantics as above; near-cap record writes fall back to a minimal record. still_open.problem: The case the finding probed is fixed and tested: a stale record whose cmd lock is free kills nothing, and command_pgid is documented in rewrite/spec/records/job.md. But the lock only proves that some process holding the inherited descriptor is alive, not that the recorded group is. A descendant that leaves the group with setsid() and keeps its descriptors holds <key>.cmd.lock after its group is gone. The next worker for that key then waits 5 s, runs without the lock, and still records command_pgid. At a later loss, the escapee's lock authorizes the SIGKILL. Probe: run 1's command started a child that forked, called setsid and slept. Run 2 of the same key, a 1-second command, took 6.3 s and recorded command_pgid. A stale running record naming an unrelated 'sleep 30' group then had that group killed (-9) on the next attach.
still_open.proposed_fix: Give each attempt a fresh cmd lock: attach, while it holds the job lock and before it spawns the worker, unlinks <key>.cmd.lock (or the lock name carries the nonce). An earlier attempt's escapee then holds only an unlinked inode and can neither delay nor authorize anything. A worker that runs without the lock records no command_pgid. Before the kill, check that the group leader is the one recorded (for example its ps start time against the record's started), or narrow the claim in records/job.md. Add a test with a descendant that calls setsid and keeps the descriptor: an unrelated group named by a stale record survives, and a re-run of the key does not wait 5 s.

still_open.problem: New, from the C1-2 fix. start() reads the record before the lock probes, and _held_answer acts on that snapshot. If the first start call writes 'running' and releases its settle lock between the read and the settle probe, the second call treats the record as stale. stop_products(subject) then stops the healthy product the first call just reported, and a second product is started. Before the fix, the second call returned the first answer (D14). Probe: _held_answer given a 'starting' copy of a running record killed the product. Two concurrent env.start calls of one subject, with the read-to-probe window widened by a sleep, both returned 0 with different pids, and the first call's product was dead.
still_open.proposed_fix: Decide on a record read after the settle probe. A live start call writes 'running' before releasing the settle lock, so only a record still 'starting' once the settle lock is free is stale. A record that now says 'running' takes the running branch. Add a test that hands _held_answer a 'starting' snapshot over a running product and asserts that the product survives and its answer is returned.

still_open.problem: New, from the C1-3 fix. Admission now refuses above RECORD_CAP - RECORD_HEADROOM (3,872 bytes), but both refusals still say the cap was exceeded. attach raises 'the record would be 3873 bytes, over the 4000-byte cap', and env.start's refusal has the same form. That is untrue for any size between the bar and the cap.
still_open.proposed_fix: Name the bar that was applied, for example 'over the 3872-byte limit (the 4000-byte cap less 128 bytes kept for later writes)', in both attach and env._launch_locked. Keep the cap in the text, and assert the message in test_record_over_the_headroom_is_refused_before_anything_is_written.
